entities.name: Social Contract Theory
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary: Political theory holding that government authority derives from a voluntary agreement among citizens. Developed by Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau, it provided intellectual justification for the American and French Revolutions and modern democratic governance.

entities.name: Social Contract Theory
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary: The theory that legitimate political authority derives from an agreement among individuals to form a society and submit to governance in exchange for protection of natural rights. Articulated by Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau, this idea became the philosophical engine of modern democracy and constitutionalism.
